label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: snowpack: There is 50-60 cm of snow above 2200 m in the Bow Summit area. The snowpack is remarkably strong, and travel is easy with no breaking through and easy track setting. No new avalanches observed. I suspect the only place to worry right now would be in steep, alpine gullies where there is localized wind loading. Ski quality was quite good, but certainly lots or rocks and other hazards lurki…

reports.title: Sugar Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Quick trip in to Sugar Bowl today. 0 degrees at the road has settled the snowpack and all creek crossings are open - we had to walk over a few but it was easy. 4 cm of new snow in the last 24 hours. The snowpack is well consolidated for being only 50 cm deep, and travel was pretty good (but rough) to get up into the bowl. Once in the bowl, the ski quality was pretty good with dry snow found…

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment:

Good day. A fresh 15-25cms all the way down to the road. (Cars turning around on the highway or not making the hills) Huge flakes on the drive up. 2c in the parking lot 930. 4c when leaving at 1500hr. Stayed around 0 most of the day at 2200m. Turned into a bit of sleet in the afternoon It was getting heavy. A nice base tho. HST ~ 60-70cms. Some…

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: Still need more snow depth to avoid any rrocks, especially at Alpine elevations subjected to wind. Snowpack held together fairly well but conditions changed rapidly with elevation. Strong winds began to pick up at the end of the day from the south by South East.

reports.title: Cirque fore Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Skied some mellow tree line slopes at Cirque fore peak. Hit the occasional rock in thin windblown areas.

60cm in the alpine where we measured. Saw no avalanche activity where we were. Wind was picking up as we left for the day.

reports.title: Observation subpeak
reports.comment: quick: Temps rose to above 0, top layer of snow below treeline very heavy. Some small movements below rock but nothing unexpected. Icy crust ~30cm down and a distinct layer ~10cm down on SW facing slopes. By mid day snow thermometer read -1.5C

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Rode SW aspect on Helen Shoulder. At ~2300m HS 60cm. Sun crust evident from 10/31/16, buried by ~5-10 cm of fresh powder from overnight snowfall. Another crust presented CT E6 SC down 25 and at the base CT M14 SC down 59cm. Fun skiing in the trees. Heard two slides on the North side of the valley but couldn't see them due to heavy fog. -1 in lot at 2:30p.m.

reports.title: Observation Subpeak
reports.comment: quick: HST- 60-70cms. Storm snow 30-40cms. Sun crust, heat crust at 30-40cms down solar aspects. Getting warmer as the day went on and windy moments coming from S / SW with spin drift. Some sign of a natural activity from the past under the storm snow.

reports.title: Bow summit area
reports.comment: snowpack: ECTN17 down 30 on a break.

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment: quick: HS 70 cm

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Storm snow on top of the Nov 12 crust wants to move on steeper slopes. Thin windslabs were forming on NE aspects. Trail to Bow hut is pretty terrible right meow.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Good riding on leeward side 75cm depth. 25cm recent snow on top of Nov 12 layer. West aspect at 2400m was very hard and difficult to skin up. Watch this layer as snow depth increases. Nov 12 layer less prevelant on leeward side, good riding did some enjoyable yoyo laps. Ride back to hwy 93 was good, but rapidly decreasing coverage below 2300.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Skiing quality was very good at Bow Summit.  High winds were experienced all day from the west or south west.  Lots of snow transport.  No slab conditions yet in the open areas tested (but not skied, we stayed in the trees), but I wouldn't be surprised if slab were forming as the wind continued.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Nice ski quality up high, although each ridge line was a little shallow. South West aspects seemed a little better than North West for coverage.
Saw 2 large natural avalanches triggered by cornice collapse on Sunday morning, within minutes of sun hitting. Temperature was still around -10C at that point, but there had just been 30+cm of snow, wind and no sun for a couple days. 
Snowpack on H…

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Good touring conditions up into the sub-alpine today.  Wx - light westerlies, periodic snow flurries, temps -10 in am warming to -5 around noon.  Felt like high humidity.  Ski pen 20cm in treed areas.  Starting to facet out in rocky areas, esp along the cliffy area.  Didn't venture far into the alpine due to low vis.  Conditions in alpine felt wind affected on west aspects.  Best skiing at …

reports.title: Observation Peak size 2 on Nov crust
reports.comment: avalanche: Initiated below cliffs as a 10 m slab which propagated to a 30 m wide slab.  Ran on the November crust.

reports.title: Photo of Observation Pk sz 2 avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: started as 10 m wide slab releasing beneath the cliffs , propagated to 30 m wide.  Ran on Nov 12 crust. (Duplicate report attached photo this time)

reports.title: Cirque Fore Peak
reports.comment: quick: Dug a pit at 2400m results were CT Hard 2 which failed on the Trump Crust at 50cm. Noticed a surface hoar.

reports.title: Helen Ridge
reports.comment: avalanche: Whiteout conditions obscured the slope steepness.  The intent was to stick to <20 degree slopes.

reports.title: Bow Summit Study Plot Profile
reports.comment: snowpack: Profile attached

reports.title: Avalanche activity
reports.comment: avalanche: Two size 2 avalanches noted today. Both were in crossloaded alpine terrain and probably occurred within the last 24 hours. One was on Dolomite Peak and another on Observation Peak.

reports.title: Bow Summit Profile
reports.comment: quick: During a flight to Skoki today we obs several natural avalanches and one cornice triggered avalanche predominantly in alpine terrain, suspect all were failing on the Dec 19 interface.

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Very wind effected, winds steady moderate-strong from the north at the ridge. Not much deposition in lees, and cornices are forming slowly. Experienced some whoomphing on thin morainal features. 150-180cm on the glacier, no new avalanches observed.

reports.title: Hellen's Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Hid from the strong winds at tree line on Helen's Ridge and found great riding in the open glades.  The upper snow pack feels hollow when trail breaking with a widespread 25cm thick soft Alan sitting over 10-15cm of low density facets above the Nov12 crust.  Ski pen was around 40cm which made for wallowing trail breaking.  Shooting cracks in steep terrain and Some recent skier triggers size…

reports.title: Bow
reports.comment: quick: We had 2 prominent layers, one being SH at  and the other a MF crust at 60cm. The MF layer was non reactive with our compression tests but we had fracture planar breaks at the SH layer, at 20 compressions. Winds picked up throughout the day and brought along a storm that roughly brought 5cms of fresh during the day.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: snowpack: Moderate 4 down 35cm resistant planar on Dec 19 facets. Moderate 5 down 90cm sudden collapse on Nov 12 layer.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades Dec 30
reports.comment:
quick: Multiple 1 and 1.5 sluff avalanches caused by overhead hazards (cornice falls primarily). 

Snow pit dug at 2150m below tree line limit 13:00 180cm snow depth. 
30cm wind deposit
27 Sudden Planar on November 12th interface. 
-12 C air temp at snow pit

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Day started off sunny with light winds but at approximately 14:30 the wind picked up to gusts. At approximately this time as well we began to notice cornice fall and  sluffing off of crowfoot mountain headwall (lookers left) but did not trigger any slides below it.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder Burn Profile
reports.comment: quick: Bottomless facets and depth hoar. Very unnerving and undesirable.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder snow profile
reports.comment: snowpack: Very weak snowpack observed in the bowl at Helen Shoulder today.  This is a very popular ski area, so keep this snowpack in mind as the winter develops and we get some additional load on top of this snowpack.  Ski quality was breaking through to near the ground.

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Despite the cold, there were af ew of us skiing treeline to just above treeline at West Nile. Saw evidence of natural avalanches, most likely a few days old from the last storm cycle. Snow was either faceted or wind blown. Pockets of rideable powder. Stayed away from wind loaded features. A bit tracked out but still lots of mellow lines to be had.

reports.title: Bow Summit Skier Accidental Size 1 - hard wind slab
reports.comment: avalanche: Stubborn hard windslabs. 2 skier accidental size 1 in Bow Summit region involving the windslab in the alpine and one whumph and slab propagation with 2 cm movement at treeline.  Would not trust any open slope at treeline or alpine for now.

reports.title: Wapta conditions
reports.comment: quick: Numerous natural size one windslabs last night observed around bow hut, with moderate to strong west winds and intense snow transport overnight and into today. One larger size two natural avalanche observed yesterday the NE face of Trapper peak <24h old. All aspects have seen wind effect and good turns are hard to come by, though travel is good.

reports.title: Cirque Peak
reports.comment: quick: Up Cirque peak today, generally very wind affected in the area, though a few good turns found on isolated W sheltered features above Helen lake. Right now the North couloir is quite thin and a 30m rappel is not sufficient to clear the rocky section without a couple moves of down climbing. Good visibility and no new avalanches observed.

reports.title: Size 1 Slide at Helen Shoulder Glades
Bow Hut Area Jan 16
reports.comment: weather: Temperatures over the past several days have risen considerably to -4C.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Skied a few runs from treeline at Bow Summit in the main area on east and north east facing slopes.  Snow was falling all day with light to moderate south wind in open areas.  Temps near -3.  Dug a pit and found the bottom half of the 130 cm snowpack to be facets. Snow was soft in all sheltered areas but unsupportive snowpack made it hard to get great turns.

reports.title: Mt. Patterson
reports.comment: incident: Heading up the first ascent portion of the Patterson climb. Noticed wind affected snow on the flats and the area we were about to climb. Pit results showed us that it was unlikely to drop down to surface. After about twenty minutes of kicking steps we heard a whumpf. We were close to each other at this point, looked for a way to get in the trees nearby. Our next movements triggered the a…

reports.title: Bow Hut approach
reports.comment: avalanche: Small slope triggered when approaching - this is one of the usual slopes skiers use to enter the canyon when exiting Bow Hut.  Small (10cm) surface slab from overnight winds, stepped down to Dec 18 facet layer, then stepped down to Nov 12 crust.  Debris pile minimal in canyon, however, had potential to use an individual into open water, of which there are many spots in canyon.

reports.title: Simpson Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Sunny bluebird day - the 140 cm snowpack was generally supportive and provided some good skiing on low angle slopes in Simpson Bowl.  At, and below treeline, the snowpack is entirely faceted. There was ample evidence of natural avalanche activity above treeline on east facing slopes from last week's storm  (see photo).
In the bowl we found 40-50 cm of firm wind slab (one finger to pencil) …

reports.title: Observation Peak
reports.comment: quick: Tricky skiing - light "eggshell" turns worked the best. Lot's of tracks above treeline and moguls below on uptrack.

reports.comment:
quick: We ski toured below the tree line and noticed a 10-20 cm thick wind slab at the tree line near bow summit. The wind slab was buried under 2 cm of fresh powder at 4 pm, and fresh snow was continuing to fall (S1). / snowpack: Wind slabs 10-20 cm thick.
Facets underneath the crust.
88 cm snow pack at parking lot.
112 cm snow pack at tree line.

reports.title: Bow Hut Headwall
reports.comment:
avalanche: Skier triggered size 1 on headwall. Slide was probably caused by fresh snow on reactive wind slab. Details below.

Bit of a late start into Bow Hut. We made it to the hut shortly after 3 with a plan to come straight out by dark. Conditions en route had a lot of red flags - snow by Num-Ti-Jah Lodge was slabby, Bow Lake was wind scoured, canyon had at least one small slab avalanche that a…

reports.title: Dolomite circuit
reports.comment:
quick: Whumphing on mellow and flat slopes up in the alpine. At times, you would be breaking trail and punch through to the mid pack only to wallow in the facets.

There was about 2-3cm new snow BTL in sheltered areas. At tree line and above the snow is best described as variable. 10cm of windslab some places and a few meters away, sastrugi as hard as ice. 

The wind surely was as strong in th…

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Myself and a small group skied up into the Little Crowfoot basin. Over all things were so bullet proof that there was very little concern or so faceted that there was no concern of avalanches. Light snow started at around 14:00, -27 at the cars and -14 at 2450m.

reports.title: Jimmy Simpson bowl/glades/slidepath
reports.comment: quick: excellent ski quality.  5to7cm new overnight (friday Feb3rd night).  snowed -1cm for most of day. Elevaation range: 2000m to 2400m.  skied glades, open alpine bowl and shorter steep shots.  Where slab was on top of the Dec facets, we stuck to conservative, supported terrain.  In places there there was no slab (entire snowpack was facets) we rode short shots up to 40degrees.  We has 'popping…

reports.title: WEST NILE (East slopes of Bow Pk)
reports.comment: quick: Would not want to be above treeline. Approx 5cm of fresh snow on a windcrust with faceted layer below.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Excellent skiing in the Crowfoot Glades -  30 to 40 cm ski pen, with good support. Lot's of recent activity from the cliffs above and soft slabs to size 2.5 on the moraine features below.

reports.title: Wapta, Bow-Petyo
reports.comment: quick: Spent 4 days on the Wapta, 9-12th. Lots of new snow and L-M winds. The ski quality was good to very good although we kept things mellow due to the white out conditions. Descending Bow canyon had to break trail down as there was 2-30 cm of storm snow, things are primed up. / avalanche: Observed large sluff from steep terrain as winds ramped up on the 12th.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: -2C when leaving the car. Dug a pit on N aspect 35 degrees at 2100m. CTM 11 RP 60cm. Sudden collapse down to Dec 19 facets when pulling on the fractured column. PST 25/90 ARR 60cm on wind crust and facets. Warm, soggy and heavy day. Storm snow is turning concrete overlaying facets. 0C upon return to the car. Definitely an upside down snowpack still. Natural 2.5 avalanche ran off of Crowfoot…

reports.title: Cirque peak outlier
reports.comment: quick: Whoomphing started at the car and continued to treeline where snow was heavily wind effected. Propogations up to 50m, knocking snow off trees. Skied well supported, low angle trees after bailing on heading into the alpine because of cloud and wind. No new natural avalanches observed.

reports.title: Dolomite Peak chutes
reports.comment:
avalanche: View from the back of Helen Shoulder ridge.

Last day of AST2, guide figured it was no more than a day old due to fracture line not being filled in at all.

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak Skier Remote Avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Felt a massive settlement while travelling along the bench at TL on Cirque Forepeak.  We noticed some remote fractures around the corner so traveled further to investigate The settlement led to a remote trigger size 3 avalanche in the main cross loaded gully.  Crown depth looked from anywhere from 50-150cm with a good portion of the lower gully getting entrained.

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Likely skier remote triggered, slab avalanche, 30m wide, failing on facets down 50-70cm and ran 40m. Slope was east facing at an elevation of 2150m and roughly 25deg. incline. Appeared to be size 1.

reports.title: N Cirque Peak naturals
reports.comment: avalanche: Several avalanches (size 1-2) were observed on Feb 21, apparently occuring on Feb 20, on the north aspect of Cirque Peak. They appeared to be the result from cornice failure from the ridge above, resulting in failure of the facet layer. At least one triggered a secondary avalanche on a convex roll much further down the slope.

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: We skied Little Crowfoot glacier yesterday.  Ski quality was good a treeline in protected areas and wind effected in open areas and in the alpine.

The day started out clear, calm and cold (-19C at valley bottom) and got progressively warmer and cloudier throughout the day.  It was -8C, overcast, with moderate to strong winds out of the west by 15:30.

Travel was excellent on a supportive b…

reports.title: Peyto area
reports.comment: quick: Numerous large whumpfs in shallow, rocky terrain on approach to hut.  Moderate to strong SW winds built wind slabs on lee aspects Feb. 23-24.  NW winds overnight Feb. 24 caused widespread hard slab and sastrugi.  50-75cm height of snow on lower Peyto glacier.  150-300cm snow coverage depending on aspect and exposure on upper Peyto glacier and icefield. / avalanche: Mt. reports.title: Wapta Icefield
reports.comment: quick: Aborted tour from Bow Hut to Guy Hut on Saturday, March 4. High winds and snow all night Friday . Saturday morning, still blowing but by 10:30 it began to calm down. We started up the Onion on our way the Guy Hut. 30-40cm of new snow on the lee features on the ascent. 10cm new wind affected snow on the neve with a few moments of good visibility. On the descent toward Mt Collie the snow and …

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: We were just finishing our AT tour at West Nile, behind the mosquito creek hostel. The temp had risen to 1 degree and the sun had been out for an hour. From the viewpoint of the road we saw a cornice drop from the ridge , trigger a release which slid to the slopes below , stopping above tree line.

reports.title: Wapta
reports.comment:
quick: Attempted Wapta traverse. Turned around below Balfour High Col due to warm stormy conditions and poor visibility. Strong winds over the last few days lead to significant wind transport. Temperatures increased to near zero on March 13th  depth of new snow was challenging to determine with the strong winds. 

Natural avalanches noted off steeper terrain, but loudy conditions limited observa…

reports.title: Bow Summit Study Plot Profile
reports.comment: snowpack: Still getting hard sudden collapse results on the December facets down 135cm in weak large depth hoar crystals. It is slowly becoming more difficult to trigger but will result in large avalanches once triggered.

reports.title: Dolomite Pass
reports.comment: quick: Dolomite loop today. Experienced a large whumph while travelling through a thin area just below profile site. Lots of avalanche activity in the area from last weeks cycle. The crux slopes on the S side of Dolomite Pass have all avalanched, filling the valley, also the slopes on your right as you approach treeline have also slid to the historical trimline...

reports.title: Helen Ridge Hike Trail Large Avy Pictures
reports.comment: quick: We show shoed  up the Helen Lake hike trail after we got lost a few times, so much snow. We turned around at the large avy area, it took out tree's as big as us. this was way before the normal open area slide area

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Went up Bow Summit today.  Good powder 15 to 30 cm of soft snow on top of nice supportive layer for good travel and fun skiing. At TL on a NE 25 deg aspect a large group kindly left a pit dug all the way to ground,  at 215cm deep,  so we stopped to do a couple tests.  Compression  test failed on facets down about 175cm: sudden planar at 18 taps.  Saw propagation test dropped about 25cm into…

reports.title: Warning for parking on shoulder of 93N
reports.comment: quick: FYI: we were ticketed for parking on the shoulder of 93N between Num Ti Jah lodge and Bow summit, a common pull over spot for skiing at Observation and Cirque peak areas. Basis for ticket was that vehicle was partly in the lane (not fully onto the shoulder due to high snow banks). Fine is $155.

reports.title: Observation Peak, North-East Glacier
reports.comment: quick: Decent to great conditions on Observation Peak (north-east glacier) and adjacent alpine slopes between Observation and Cirque Peak north glacier. Wind affected but still better than Netflix! No signs of recent slab avalanches, however the steep convex roll above the Observation glacier (~ 2900 m, NE aspect, wind loaded) looks like it went at about size 2 based on debris in the bowl below (c…

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Rode treeline and alpine area above West Nile trees just east of Grand daddy couloir. Melt crust in the trees on the way up with 5 to 10 cm of fresh snow. Treeline and alpine conditions were great. Couple old slides were observed. No recent avalanche activity observed. Snow turned heavy in the trees as the day went on and the temps went up. Still great snow to be found at higher elevations!

reports.title: Little Crowfoot Glacier
reports.comment: quick: Cornice triggered size 2 off the rock wall on climbers right - very recent deposit. Excellent travel and skiing conditions on cold North aspects.

reports.title: Mt. Jimmy SImpson
reports.comment: avalanche: Report from two people skiing up the moraines on the ascent of Jimmy Simpson, triggered a surprising avalanche on top of a moraine.  20-40 cm deep (max 70 cm) by 120m wide on a 25-30 degree slope - did not run far, the slope slumped and ran a short distance. Past week's storm snow settled into a slab over sun crust.  Partial burial, no injuries - party dug out and moved on.
